summary: This Wikipedia-derived note describes the British Isles as a group of islands covering the United Kingdom and Ireland, with shared cultural life (media, reality TV, book and music awards), a common history of kingdoms and Tudor-era church separation, and a geology shaped by ancient mountain-building. It also covers shared sports and rugby competitions, population distribution, cross-border parliamentary bodies, and the limited reptile and amphibian fauna of Great Britain and Ireland.
one_line: Overview of the British Isles, covering shared media and culture, geology, sport, population, cross-border bodies and wildlife.
key_facts: Irish newspapers are available in the UK, and Irish state and private television is widely available in Northern Ireland.
The X Factor seasons 3, 4 and 7 featured auditions in Dublin and were open to Irish voters.
The Costa Book Awards are awarded to authors resident in the UK or Ireland.
The Man Booker Prize is awarded to authors from the Commonwealth of Nations and Ireland.
The Mercury Music Prize is handed out every year to the best album from a British or Irish musician or group.
In 1534 King Henry VIII separated from the Roman Church after failing to secure a divorce from the Pope.
The Caledonian Orogeny during the Ordovician Period, c. 488–444 Ma, formed the mountains and hills of northern Britain and Ireland when the craton Baltica collided with the terrane Avalonia.
Over the last 500 million years the land forming the British Isles drifted northwest from around 30°S, crossing the equator around 370 million years ago.
Many globally popular sports had modern rules codified in the British Isles, including golf, association football, cricket, rugby, snooker and darts.
The British and Irish Lions is a team chosen from each national team and undertakes tours of the southern hemisphere rugby playing nations every four years.
Since 2001 the professional club teams of Ireland, Scotland, Wales and Italy compete against each other in the RaboDirect Pro12.
England accounts for almost 80% of the total population of the British Isles, and the Greater London Urban Area has 9 million inhabitants.
The British–Irish Parliamentary Assembly was established in 1990 and originally comprised 25 members of the Oireachtas and 25 members of the parliament of the United Kingdom.
Only three snakes are native to Great Britain: the common European adder, the grass snake and the smooth snake; none are native to Ireland.
Few species of reptiles or amphibians are found in Great Britain or Ireland, and Great Britain has slightly more native wildlife than Ireland.
